parts.title: Plan a weekend away
parts.instructions: Read what each person is looking for. Match each person to the best activity. There are three extra activities.

people.text: Anouk has never been on a boat and would like to try something on the water on Saturday morning.
Bruno loves old streets and castles and wants a guided tour so that he can hear stories about the town.
Cleo is travelling with two young children and needs a free activity for a rainy day.
Dmitri enjoys good food and wants to taste dishes made with local ingredients.
Esme is very active and wants a long walk with great views of the coast.

texts.title: Old town walking tour
texts.text: Follow a local guide through narrow streets and hear stories about the castle, the harbour and the market. Tours leave daily at 11 a.m. and last 90 minutes.

texts.title: Family library morning
texts.text: Rainy day? Come to the town library for free story time, drawing and games for children under ten. Open all weekend.

texts.title: Beginner kayaking
texts.text: Never paddled before? Our friendly instructors will teach you the basics on the calm bay. Saturday and Sunday mornings, equipment included.

texts.title: Pottery workshop
texts.text: Make your own cup or plate in a two-hour class. Choose your colours and we will post your work to you after it has been fired.

texts.title: Harbour food market
texts.text: Taste cheese, fish and bread from nearby farms and boats. You can watch cooks prepare dishes and try them before you buy. Saturdays only.

texts.title: Stars from the hill
texts.text: Join our astronomer on the hilltop to look at the stars. The evening starts at 10 p.m. on clear nights.

texts.title: Cliff path walk
texts.text: Walk twelve kilometres along the high cliffs and enjoy views of the whole coast. Wear strong shoes; there are no cafés on the way.

texts.title: Lighthouse museum
texts.text: Learn how sailors used the lighthouse and climb to the top. Open 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., but closed on Mondays.

parts.title: A weekend by the sea
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my cousin invited me to spend a weekend in a small seaside town. We travelled by coach because it was cheaper than the train, although the journey took longer. When we arrived, the weather was cloudy, so we visited the local museum first. I expected it to be rather boring, but a guide showed us old photographs of the harbour and explained how the fishing boats had changed over time.

The next morning was sunny. We hired bicycles and followed a path along the coast. The route was mostly flat, but we stopped several times to take photographs. At lunchtime, we bought sandwiches from a small shop and ate them on the beach. It was busy, but we found a quiet place near the rocks.

On Sunday, we planned to take a boat trip. Unfortunately, the sea was too rough, so the trip was cancelled. The owner gave everyone a refund and suggested a walk to a lighthouse instead. I was disappointed at first, but the view from the top was wonderful. I would happily return, especially if I could stay for a few more days.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer travel by coach?
questions.explanation: The coach was cheaper than the train, so it was less expensive.

questions.prompt: What surprised the writer at the museum?
questions.explanation: She expected the museum to be boring, but the guide showed interesting old photographs, so she was surprised how interesting it was.

questions.prompt: What did they do on the coast path?
questions.explanation: They stopped several times to take photographs along the coast path.

questions.prompt: Why was the boat trip cancelled?
options: The weather at sea was unsafe.
questions.explanation: The sea was too rough, so the weather at sea was unsafe.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about the weekend?
options: They did not enjoy the town.
They would like a longer visit.
They want to travel by train next time.
questions.explanation: She says she would happily return and stay for a few more days, so she would like a longer visit.

parts.title: The coastal path
parts.instructions: Five sentences have been removed from the text. Choose the correct sentence for each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage: The coastal path is popular with visitors and local people, especially in spring and summer. [1] It begins near the old harbour and continues past a small museum. [2] The town has added signs so walkers can find the route easily, and volunteers clean the path every month. There are benches at several points, and most of the path is flat. [3] Some families bring a picnic and stop beside the beach. Dogs are welcome, but they must stay on a lead near the farms. The final section goes uphill towards a lighthouse. [4] On clear days, you can see several islands from the top. The council hopes to extend the path next year. [5]
sentences: It is steep in places, but the climb is worth it.
It is about eight kilometres long and takes most people three hours.
More walkers would then be able to reach the next village on foot.
Many walkers stop there to look at old photographs of the harbour.
This makes it a good walk for families with young children.
We decided to stay indoors all afternoon.

gaps.explanation: “It is about eight kilometres long” gives the first facts about the path and leads to “It begins near the old harbour”.
“Many walkers stop there to look at old photographs” follows “a small museum” (“there”) and leads to the signs.
“This makes it a good walk for families” follows “most of the path is flat” and leads to families bringing a picnic.
“It is steep in places, but the climb is worth it” follows the uphill section and leads to the view from the top.
“More walkers would then be able to reach the next village” follows the hope to extend the path.

The station is [4] the town centre, so visitors can walk to the shops. If it rains, you can [5] the local museum. Children usually enjoy the journey as much as the destination. parts.title: A day at the coast
parts.instructions: Complete the text with one word in each gap.
parts.passage: We arrived [1] the coast before lunchtime. The weather was warmer [2] we had expected, so we left our coats in the car. My sister wanted to swim, [3] the water was too cold. We spent an hour looking [4] the boats in the harbour. After lunch we walked along the beach and collected shells. Later, we found a café [5] served fresh sandwiches. It was a day [6] we will remember for a long time.

gaps.explanation: We say “arrive at” a place such as the coast.
“Warmer than we had expected” is a comparison.
“But” shows the contrast between wanting to swim and the cold water.
“Looking at the boats” means watching them.
“That” refers to the café and begins the clause “that served fresh sandwiches”.
“Which” (or “that”) refers to the day and begins the clause about remembering it.

turns.text: Welcome to the Hilltop Hostel. The front door is locked after eleven, so please take your key with you. Breakfast is served in the dining room from half past seven. parts.title: An interview with a hostel owner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Carlos, why did you open a hostel?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: I travelled a lot when I was young, and I always stayed in hostels. I met so many interesting people that I wanted to create the same friendly atmosphere in my own town.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you choose the building?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: It used to be a fish factory near the harbour. It was cheap and it had lots of space, so I painted the walls and bought second-hand beds.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What is the hardest part of the job?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: Summer weekends. Every bed is full, and guests often arrive earlier than expected. I’ve learned to keep a few clean rooms ready, just in case.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do guests enjoy most?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: The roof terrace. People sit there in the evening, share food and plan the next day. Many of them make new friends.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How has the business done?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: It took me two years before it made any money, but now we are busy from May to October.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What advice would you give someone who wants to open a hostel?

turns.speaker: carlos
turns.text: Visit lots of places first and ask guests what they like. That is the best way to learn.

questions.prompt: Why did Carlos open a hostel?

questions.explanation: Carlos says he wanted to create the same friendly atmosphere he found in hostels as a traveller.

questions.prompt: What is difficult about summer weekends?

questions.prompt: What do guests enjoy most?

questions.prompt: What does Carlos say about making money?
